source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 9.11 with Fig. 9.21 (PDF 209-210).

blocks.text: Current wale conductor ka ek hissa (segment) lein jis ki length (lambai) L aur cross-section ka area A hai. Is hisse ka volume AL hai (Fig. 9.21). Maan lein har unit volume mein n charge carriers hain; to is hisse mein kisi bhi waqt kul nAL charge carriers hain. Agar har carrier par charge q ho to hisse ke andar kul charge:

blocks.alt: Length L ka conductor ka hissa, daen sire par oval cross-section. Andar dairay wale negative charges, hare teer baen taraf; daen sire se bahar teer I daen taraf.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.21: negative (manfi) charge carriers (kitab ki Figure 9.21 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Electrons baen taraf sarakte (drift karte) hain, is liye current I daen taraf hai. Hisse ka volume AL aur us mein kul charge Q = nALq hai.
Aam taur par conductor mein charge carriers free electrons hote hain jin par negative charge hota hai.

blocks.title: Kya aap jaante hain? (Do You Know?)
blocks.text:
• Current ka flow (bahao) potential difference ke directly proportional (seedha tanasub) hai.
• Heat ka flow temperature difference (farq) ke directly proportional hai.
• Fluid (liquid ya gas) ka flow pressure difference ke directly proportional hai.

blocks.title: Maloomat ke liye (For Your Information)
blocks.text: Current charge ka flow (bahao) hai: voltage use chalne par majboor karta hai aur resistance use rokti hai.

Maan lein conductor par potential difference lagane se charge carriers hisse ke baen (left) siray ki taraf chalte hain. Tab current daen (right) siray ki taraf hota hai. Agar carriers ki drift velocity v ho to hisse mein shuru se maujood saare carriers ko baen siray se nikalne mein waqt:
Q aur t ki qeematein rakhne se:

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: I = nAvq batata hai ke current char cheezon par depend karti hai: carriers kitne ghane hain (n), taar kitna mota hai (A), carriers kitni tezi se sarakte hain (v), aur har carrier par kitna charge hai (q).

blocks.title: Example (kitab mein 9.6)
blocks.problem: Copper ke taar ka cross-sectional area 2 × 10⁻⁶ m² hai aur us mein 3 A current hai. Agar har unit volume mein electrons ki number (ginti) 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ ho to electrons ki drift velocity nikalein. Electron ka charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C hai.
steps: Diya gaya: I = 3 A, A = 2 × 10⁻⁶ m², n = 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³, q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, v = ?
Formula: I = nAvq, is liye v = I/(nAq)
blocks.answer: v = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ (yani taqreeban 0.1 mm har second: bohat dheemi)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is example ko dobara "Example 9.6" ka number deti hai, halanke 9.6 (electron volt) mein pehle hi Example 9.6 hai; is ka apna number hona chahiye. Sawal mein "elections" chhapa hai; murad electrons hai. Solution (hal) theek hai.

blocks.prompt: Copper ke taar par potential difference lagaya gaya hai. Free electrons ki drift velocity par kya asar hoga agar (i) potential difference barhaya jaye, (ii) taar ki length aur temperature kam kiye jayein (constructed response 9.5)?
blocks.explanation: (i) Zyada potential difference taar ke andar zyada strong (taqatwar) field E = V/L deta hai, is liye collisions (takkar) ke darmiyan electrons ko zyada zor se dhakela jata hai aur drift velocity barhti hai. (ii) Usi potential difference par chhote taar mein field zyada hoti hai, is liye drift velocity barhti hai; kam temperature par lattice ke atoms kam hilte hain, collisions kam hote hain aur drift velocity aur barh jati hai.

items: Length L, area A, har unit volume mein n carriers, har ek par charge q: Q = nALq (9.29).
Carriers t = L/v mein nikal jate hain, is liye I = nAvq (9.30).
Copper ki misal: v = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹.
